gap: No result ChatGPT got says that, on BLUETTI's US store on 2026-11-14, the 2,073.6 Wh Elite 200 V2 sold with the BLUETTI Charger 1 (up to 560 W while the van is driving) costs $1,099. That is $100 less than the same station with one 200 W panel ($1,199) and $350 less than EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Max Plus + 800W Alternator Charger bundle ($1,449).
standout_why: I compared it against powersized.com/best/rv (cited), ecosolarkits.com best-rv-solar-kits (cited) and solarpowerauditor.com best-power-station-rv-van (cited). Powersized prices the stations only, with no panels. It lists the Charger 1 on its own at $299 (as of Oct 27), but BLUETTI's store shows $219 today, and it never prices a station and alternator charger together. Ecosolarkits picks the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 + Alternator Charger at $1,369.99, but lists it as sold out (Nov 9), so it has part of this finding but no bundle you can buy. Solarpowerauditor picks the Elite 200 V2 at $1,199 list (checked Sep 5) and says alternator charging needs a separately fitted DC-DC charger. It doesn't mention BLUETTI's own bundle. I couldn't read solargenadvisor.com because of a TLS certificate error.
decides: This confirms the Elite 200 V2 as the pick and changes how to sell it. For a van, the Elite 200 V2 + Charger 1 bundle ($1,099) should lead instead of the + 200 W panel kit ($1,199). It costs less and refills the battery while driving (about 3.7 h from empty at 560 W). Add a panel later if needed: the Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit costs $1,499. EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Max Plus + 800 W is the runner-up for people who drive less: about 2.6 h from empty, but $350 more. The page's EcoFlow row also needs fixing. The store can be read now, and the 800 W charger is $269, not 'about $599'. The AC180 row's 'back late Nov' is also out of date: it shows as available at $499.
